Geopolitics & Diplomacy
• US politics enters a volatile phase after Democratic midterm gains: Trump named Stephen Miller chief of staff, setting up clashes with Congress, while analysts weigh how a Democratic-led legislature could steer Ukraine support and constrain foreign policy moves toward Iran.
• In Latin America, Paraguay’s president Santiago Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest after a banking collapse froze access for millions.
• Israel’s inconclusive vote puts Arab-led parties in a potential kingmaker role, and New Zealand heads into a cliffhanger election with minor parties pivotal.
• US–China tensions sharpened as Washington warned Beijing to meet Busan trade deal terms on critical materials, China vowed retaliation over new US sanctions, and US intelligence linked a Chinese spy effort to Nvidia’s CEO.
• Europe opened a fraud probe into EU rail funds after Spain’s Urda disaster that killed 69 people.
Why it matters: From Washington to Wellington, shifting power dynamics are reshaping alliances, economic ties and security decisions that will reverberate through trade, tech and conflict zones.

Why it matters: Health systems face simultaneous biological and cyber threats, while emerging research continues to reshape prevention, regulation and care priorities.

Society & Human Rights
• Immigration and rights flashpoints intensified: Houston’s mayor curbed cooperation with ICE; Trump’s elevation of Stephen Miller drew bipartisan condemnation; and the UK Home Office faces a lawsuit over stripping 1,500 EU citizens of settled rights.
• Digital platforms under scrutiny as researchers accused TikTok of normalizing the sex industry via covert marketing tactics.
• Accountability and justice: Kenya’s doomsday cult leader received a 200-year sentence; Russell Brand’s barrister self-reported to a watchdog after confronting a reporter.
• Campus and faith debates continued with Cornell faculty’s no-confidence vote and a case highlighting Jehovah’s Witness transfusion rules changing too late for a patient.
• Culture and activism: Tallinn’s film festival reiterated solidarity with Ukraine, while Macklemore said US arenas rejected his pro-Palestine benefit tour.
Why it matters: Rights, governance and platform accountability are converging in ways that test legal frameworks and social cohesion across democracies.

Artificial Intelligence
• Post-midterm headwinds hit the AI buildout—data center restrictions advanced and stocks slid—yet industry leaders remained bullish as OpenAI reportedly raised another $11B at a $1.25T valuation and Microsoft consolidated infrastructure partners.
• Consumer AI expanded with Amazon letting users text Alexa to shop and Meta’s Muse “Spaces” building custom mini-apps; AI caregiving tools are growing but may not solve caregiver burnout.
• Security concerns deepened as hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools were exposed online, reports found free Chinese models highly capable at cyber tasks, and data brokers sought corporate files to train models.
• Robotics and autonomy accelerated: a humanoid cleaning service made headlines, and Elon Musk appeared to pivot away from Cybertruck to prioritize driverless “Cybercabs.”
• Infrastructure and economics showed strain: Crusoe sold a troubled data center project to Google; spending growth appears to be stalling per Ramp data; a METR report warned Anthropic’s automated AI development is rapidly accelerating.
Why it matters: AI’s rapid diffusion is colliding with political, security and infrastructure limits, even as capital continues to chase transformative growth.

• Markets watch inflation and Fed path next week, and India’s bourses hold a special Diwali trading session.
Why it matters: Markets are recalibrating expectations for AI returns while commodity and policy signals add crosswinds to global risk appetite.

Why it matters: Overlapping kinetic, cyber and infrastructure threats are straining civilian safety and security services from the Middle East to Europe.

• Scientists flagged a dry-soil/high-pressure feedback behind mega-heatwaves and an unprecedented early polar vortex disruption; El Niño-linked storms toppled a famed New Mexico rock spire.
• Communities face mounting impacts—from Nepal’s flood rebuilding and Sudanese child malnutrition to a climate–debt “doom loop.”
• Infrastructure policy and tech demand intersect as a US permitting bill to speed energy projects advances and AI data centers stir environmental fights; guidance urged safer Diwali celebrations amid hazardous air.
• A rare baby right whale discovery off Canada offered a conservation bright spot.
Why it matters: With climate hazards intensifying, policy choices on oceans, mountains, energy and infrastructure will determine resilience and equity outcomes.

Science & Technology.title: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?
Science & Technology.text: Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.  NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASAThe tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.“I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”Why Phobos Is Such a Strange MoonPhobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites. The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASAScientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.More than 10 years in the making, MMX launched on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA. Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXAMMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.If all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth. The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.How MMX Will Orbit Phobos An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty ImagesOnce MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.“If something doesn’t go according to plan, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.Martian ManeuversThe best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.Idefix Rover: The First PenguinBefore the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu says, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.  MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXAIt will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict. The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR“It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.  A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”  The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLRThe team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.  With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/AlamyIdefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”What Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.How MMX Will Land and Collect SamplesOnce Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.  MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXAThe pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.  After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXADuring the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.  MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXAFinally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.“MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

Entertainment.title: Alpha Industries x No Problemo Map Mount Kailash Across the CWU-45 Jacket
Entertainment.text: SummaryAlpha Industries and No Problemo reunite for FW26, moving from the MA-1 of their first collaboration to the CWU-45 flight jacketThe sage green jacket keeps the CWU-45’s fold-down collar, high-set pockets and structured shapeGraphics from No Problemo’s “Mount Kailash” collection cover the back, and tonal branding runs along the sleeveAlpha Industries and No Problemo have released the Alpha Industries x No Problemo CWU-45, the second chapter of a partnership that started with a take on the MA-1. Finished in sage green for FW26, the jacket brings the graphic world of No Problemo’s Mount Kailash collection to one of Alpha’s most structured military silhouettes.The CWU-45 was first issued to Air Force and Navy pilots in 1972, and its build is very different from the MA-1 the brands reworked last time. A fold-down collar replaces the bomber’s ribbed neck, the pockets sit higher on the body and the overall cut is more structured. The collaboration keeps all three features, using them as the base for No Problemo’s graphic treatment instead of redesigning the jacket.Most of the change happens on the back panel, where hand-drawn figures, symbols and abstract shapes spread across the full width of the jacket. The artwork comes from Mount Kailash, No Problemo’s FW26 collection, which draws on the myths, geometric patterns and charged atmosphere associated with the 6,666-meter Tibetan peak. Against the muted sage base, the line work reads like a coded map more than a typical back print.The branding is more restrained elsewhere on the jacket. No Problemo’s logo runs down one sleeve in a tonal finish that blends into the base color, while a co-branded patch on the chest marks the collaboration. Alpha Industries’ signature red Remove Before Flight tag completes the jacket and adds the only bright color to an otherwise subdued palette.The Alpha Industries x No Problemo CWU-45 will be available online, via the Alpha Industries store in Frankfurt, Aries, Aries Soho in London and select retailers.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Barbour x Paraboot Trade Waxed Canvas and French Leather for FW26
Entertainment.text: SummaryBarbour and Paraboot reunite seven years after their first collaboration with a Bedale jacket and a Chambord derbyEach piece borrows a signature material from its partner, putting olive waxed canvas on the shoe and Paraboot leather on the jacketA co-branded medallion, leather tassel and Barbour tartan lining connect the two designsBarbour and Paraboot have teamed up again for Fall/Winter 2026, pairing a reworked Bedale jacket with a Chambord derby that each take on materials from the other house. The two-piece capsule is the brands’ second collaboration, arriving seven years after their first, and it focuses on construction and craft rather than a broad product lineup.The capsule rests on a straightforward exchange of materials, with each piece lending a signature fabric to the other so the jacket and shoes read as a matched set. The British waxed canvas goes onto the French footwear, and the French leather moves onto the British outerwear, so neither design is just a logo swap.Paraboot’s piece starts from the Chambord, a flat-top derby the house first made for city wear in Paris over 40 years ago. Its core construction stays the same, with five eyelets, a full leather lining, a Norwegian welt finished with a square-edged welt, and a rubber sole. The upper changes, mixing brown “gringo” nubuck with olive waxed canvas taken directly from Barbour’s jacket language.The finishing details make the shoe clearly a collaboration. A co-branded medallion and a leather tassel, both made specifically for this release, hang from the laces, and Barbour’s classic tartan lines the interior. Every pair comes in a Paraboot box with a matching co-branded tartan dust bag inside.Barbour’s half reworks the Bedale in Oban waxed canvas, given a brushed finish meant to build character over time. The jacket keeps its usual roomy cut, low gusseted pockets and corduroy collar, while Paraboot leather forms the chest pocket and both brand names are embroidered on the lower pockets. The same medallion and tassel from the derby appear on the jacket, and the tartan shows under the collar and across the lining.That tartan is what ties the capsule together, running through the collar, the jacket lining, the inside of the shoe and its dust bag. As a result, the Bedale and the Chambord work as a coordinated pair when worn together, while each still holds up as a standalone piece.The Barbour x Paraboot collection is available now via Paraboot’s website and Barbour’s webstore, and at select Paraboot stores in Paris (Rivoli and Saint-Honoré), Versailles, Lille and Tours.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Clive Christian’s “Uncovered” Perfume Hides a Warm Heart Beneath an Icy Exterior
Entertainment.text: SummaryClive Christian unveils "Uncovered," its first transparent perfume, crafted by Elise Pierre.The floral musk shifts from icy aldehydes and eucalyptus to warm immortelle, orris and amber.A sculpted clear glass bottle and ice-block box complete its cold-to-warm story.Clive Christian’s "Uncovered", the house’s first transparent perfume, unfolds like the moment frost gives way to morning light. Selected from 14 competing compositions at the CPL Fragrance House Conference, perfumer Elise Pierre’s floral musk opens with a crisp, almost glacial brightness. Sparkling aldehydes and cool eucalyptus reach the senses first, sharpened by a flicker of pink pepper and lifted by the sunny tang of bergamot. Picture a winter window as the sun breaks through: clean, bracing and quietly inviting a closer look.As that initial chill recedes, the fragrance reveals a warmer core. Immortelle absolute lends a honeyed, sun-dried richness, while powdery orris and creamy ylang oil round out the edges, and a salty accord adds an intimate, skin-close quality. The drydown settles into white musk, sandalwood, moss and amber, glowing slowly like embers seen through clear glass. Composed at a 40% concentration from 164 ingredients, the scent is built around the idea of quiet self-revelation, appearing simple at first impression yet continuing to unveil new layers the longer it rests on the skin.The packaging completes this story of a cool exterior concealing inner warmth. "Uncovered" is presented in a sculpted, crystal-clear glass flacon with nothing to obscure what lies inside, a vessel meant to reflect its wearer as both vulnerable and resilient. Its outer box takes the form of a block of ice, turning the act of unwrapping into a kind of thaw that leads to the treasure beneath.Unveiled as a limited edition for the holiday season, the 50 ml fragrance retails for $500 USD in the US and is available from November 15, 2026 through January 2027, or while stock lasts, at Clive Christian boutiques, select retailers worldwide and clivechristian.com.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Balenciaga Hires Martine Rose & Yeezy Makes Runway Return in This Week's Top Fashion News
Entertainment.text: SummaryMartine Rose took the helm at Balenciaga, while Ralph Lauren secured top menswear honors at the 2026 CFDA Awards.Ye announced a Yeezy reboot in Los Angeles, and the 2027 Met Gala revealed a new, everyday-focused theme.Palace detailed its Burberry collaboration, and Joaquin Phoenix debuted smart eyewear with Gentle Monster.Martine Rose Confirmed at Balenciaga' a Day After Piccioli ExitFollowing widespread speculation, Martine Rose was officially named the new creative director of Balenciaga. The London-based designer will oversee all men's and women's collections moving forward. Rose brings her signature subcultural edge to the heritage luxury house, signaling a new shift in Balenciaga's aesthetic trajectory. Her debut collection is expected to hit the runway next season, where she will establish her updated vision for the brand. The appointment arrived only one day after it was confirmed that Pierpaolo Piccioli would step down from the role.Ye Presents Yeezy Season 01 Runway Show in Los AngelesYe presented a brand new Yeezy Season 01 runway show in Los Angeles on the evening of November 4. A complete reset for the apparel line, the runway returned to the designer’s foundational utilitarian aesthetics, revisiting silhouettes and details. The new lineup featured boxy proportions, washed earth tones, heavy layering, and stripped-down footwear with zero overt branding. Standing out were pairs of translucent footwear, gigantic duffle bags, and all-red numbers.The Met Gala 2027 Pivots Theme for Exhibition: "Extraordinary Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday"The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced a pivot for its 2027 Costume Institute exhibition and Met Gala theme. Titled "Extraordinary Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday," the upcoming event highlights the intersection of mundane daily wear and high fashion. The shift suggests a departure from historical archiving in favor of exploring how ordinary objects and routine garments inform avant-garde design. It follows the abrupt cancellation of the previously selected theme, which centered on John Galliano, citing his past controversial remarks.Ralph Lauren Wins American Menswear Designer of the Year at 2026 CFDA AwardsFor a third year, American menswear icon Ralph Lauren took home the American Menswear Designer of the Year trophy at the 2026 CFDA Awards. The veteran designer was recognized for his sustained impact on American tailoring and sportswear over the past year. This latest accolade adds to Lauren's extensive list of industry honors, reaffirming his label's dominant position in the domestic menswear market and his ability to iterate on classic prep staples. The news arrived at a timely moment, as reports of Ralph Lauren topping its Q2 forecasts and raising its outlook surfaced shortly after.Palace Skateboards  x Burberry Drops Exclusively at Palace's New London Flagship Palace Skateboards has released the highly anticipated Burberry collaboration. The collection launched exclusively at Palace's brand-new Poland Street flagship in London. Blending the skate brand's signature streetwear graphics with Burberry's heritage outerwear and check patterns, the capsule bridges two distinct eras of British style. Standout pieces include a plaid overcoat and hooded jacket emblazoned with the Palace x Burberry emblem, and a toile-inspired trench with matching graphics.Gentle Monster Taps Joaquin Phoenix for Intelligent Eyewear CampaignActor Joaquin Phoenix partnered with South Korean brand Gentle Monster to launch a new line of intelligent eyewear. The collaboration integrates smart technology directly into the frames without compromising the sleek, futuristic silhouettes Gentle Monster is known for. The full campaign film premieres later this month, and pre-orders for the Intelligent Eyewear Collection open on November 12. A public preview will also take place in New York City from November 13 to 23, with registration available through Gentle Monster’s official website.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: The 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Custom In-Game Cars Have Come to Life
Entertainment.text: SummaryWest Coast Customs helped recreate the in-game custom cars of 'Grand Theft Auto VI'Each car comes with its own backstory, including stats, figures and details'Grand Theft Auto VI' finally arrives on November 19Grand Theft Auto VI is finally coming, and one of the best, most detailed components of the game is coming to life. Literally.The iconic West Coast Customs of Los Angeles was brought in to recreate some of the most recognizable in-game cars with real life counterparts. The detail that went into replicating the replicas must have been painstaking, as we even had a bit of difficulty differentiating the in-game shots (above) from the real life photos (below). And what's even better is that each car is baked with stats and IRL figures, bridging their digital and real-life connections even stronger. Ever wonder what the engine was under the Coquette? Or how much horsepower the Tempesta cop car has? Check out the breakdown of each car and judge for yourself how close each car got to its in-game version. Grotti CheetahThe Grotti Cheetah is quintessentially Miami. The classic mid-engined ’90s supercar is clean, with Italian-styled lines broken only by intakes feeding a 4.9L naturally-aspirated V8. West Coast Customs lowered it on track-ready tires, gave it a “Vice City fade” paint job, and trimmed the cabin with custom-stitched Italian leather.Albany BuccaneerThe Buccaneer is a fully restored 1960s lowrider with a 7.5L V8, paired with hits of mahogany and gold trim throughout. The candy apple green paint, laid down in large metallic flake, carries bespoke airbrushing and pinstripes for the ultimate custom look. Air-ride suspension and gold multi-spoke rims sit under a cream ragtop and a leather interior with zebra-print inlays, because Vice City.Progen EmerusPerhaps the wildest build in this list, the Emerus is a track-ready thoroughbred, with aero bodywork and fighter jet-style vents built around a twin-turbo 4.0L V8. It’s painted candy orange with an even louder orange interior to match. One of the largest aero wings on the market, plus custom suspension and racing tires, keeps it planted when you're five-star and on the run.Invetero CoquetteThe icon and probably most recognizable. The mid-engined Coquette packs a 6.2L naturally aspirated V8 we all secretly know and love. Its “Yeti Camo” livery for the game in flamingo pink and vibrant purple definitely stands out in your garage. It also gets custom rims, lowered suspension and a fully custom leather interior.Albany MananaThe Manana is a 1970s classic with a 7.7L V8, stripped down and rebuilt with bold, straight panels for a fresh take on donk. It’s coated in large-flake Vice City blue paint with gold bumpers and trim. A sky-high custom suspension sits on oversized gold-and-chrome rims, and the matching blue leather cabin is edged in gold for added flair.Pegassi TempestaThe aggressive, mid-engined Invetero Tempesta runs a flame-spitting 4.0L naturally aspirated V10. It wears a Vice Beach Police Department livery over lowered suspension and custom rims, because even one time deserve some style. Inside, the cockpit takes after a fighter jet, packed with custom leather, buttons and cutting edge police tech. All we have to say is: good luck.Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: The Kith x New Balance 2011 “Monuments” Collection Builds New York Landmarks Into Every Panel
Entertainment.text: Name: Kith x New Balance 2011Colorway: Maroon/Atomic Yellow, Amazon/Lilac, Princess Blue/SilverSKU: TBCMSRP: TBCRelease Date: November 9Where to Buy: KithKith and New Balance are returning to the 2011 for the Monuments Collection, a trio of colorways that each salute one of New York City’s most recognizable landmarks. The silhouette first surfaced earlier this year as part of Kith’s 15-year anniversary run, and its name points straight back to the year the retailer opened its doors. This time around, the city’s skyline does the storytelling while the materials do the heavy lifting.Under every colorway sits the same architecture. Kith built the 2011 upper from the ground up, assembling a layered, multi-piece pattern rather than adapting an existing New Balance last, then set it atop the ABZORB midsole unit originally developed for the New Balance 2002. That combination gives the shoe a familiar, cushioned ride underneath a construction that is entirely its own, leaving each Monuments colorway free to play with texture and finish.The “Maroon & Atomic Yellow” pair carries the deepest Kith lineage, revisiting the Ronnie Fieg for New Balance 530 that dropped at Kith in 2014. Perforated nubuck forms the base, layered with perforated nubuck and leather overlays and finished with quilted stitching across the vamp and collar. A full-bleed debossed 2011 graphic covers the heel, contrasting N-lock logos land on both sides, and silver-flecked laces add a subtle shimmer, with additional branding placed on the tongue and heel counter.The “Amazon & Lilac” iteration takes a bolder color-blocked route, built from perforated suede overlays on top of suede underlays. Reflective N-logos on the lateral and medial walls catch light after dark, while dual New Balance and Kith branding sits on the tongue and heel, and 2011 hits mark the outer ankle.Rounding out the set, the “Princess Blue & Silver” version swaps to a breathable mesh base dressed in vibrant suede overlays. Orange accents at the eyelets, N-logos and heel branding cut through the cool palette, joined by a co-branded tongue and 2011 detailing at the lateral heel. All three pairs arrive in New York to the World packaging, finished with a custom sockliner and an extra set of laces.Set your reminders and get ahead of what’s dropping next on Hypebeast Drops.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Kia’s EV4 GT Clay Concept Is the Ultimate Tribute to Rafael Nadal
Entertainment.text: With 63 clay-court titles under his belt, Rafael Nadal’s reputation as the undisputed "King of Clay" has brought his legacy beyond tennis to fashion and lifestyle. Now, Korean car brand Kia is honoring the acclaimed player with a one-of-a-kind concept befitting his nickname. The full-scale EV4 GT clay concept features a top-to-bottom transformation, where the doors, bonnet, and windows are all dressed in a red-orange tone. Enhancing the court inspiration, white lines run across the angular edges, matching the white inscribed signature on the back and Kia logo.In an official statement, Rafael Nadal shared, “Kia has been by my side throughout my career, through all the highs and the challenges. Receiving this tribute, created from the material that has defined so much of my journey, is incredibly meaningful. It is a special reminder of everything we have shared, and I am honored by this gesture.”Commemorating a partnership that has lasted more than two decades, the clay concept provides a joint tribute to the player’s career as well as the innovation Kia has focused on over that time. A closer look at the car reveals how these two worlds have been brought together, with a blend of tennis court clay and automotive modelling clay. This combination gives the car a unique texture that's tactile while subtly matted. As the model reinforces Kia’s commitment to “movement that inspires,” Soohang Chang, President and CEO of Kia Europe, shared, “Rafael’s determination and resilience have inspired tennis players and fans around the world, and those values have been central to our partnership since 2004.” “This tribute celebrates Rafael’s remarkable achievements and the journey we have shared. Through tennis and our wider sporting partnerships, Kia aims to bring people together and inspire future generations,” he adds. Discover the car in the images shot at the Rafa Nadal Academy in Mallorca.To find out more about the Kia EV4 GT, head to the brand’s website now.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Superblue Kyoto to Open in Early 2027 With Landmark James Turrell Exhibition
Art & Culture.text: SummarySuperblue has announced its first international art center Superblue Kyoto opening in early 2027The venue will inaugurate with a major long-term solo exhibition by Light and Space artist James TurrellLocated directly opposite teamLab Biovortex Kyoto the indigo-clad space will announce full programming details in DecemberExperiential art company Superblue has officially announced the opening of Superblue Kyoto, launching its first international venue in Japan in early 2027 with a major solo exhibition by Light and Space pioneer James Turrell. Situated directly across from teamLab Biovortex Kyoto in the Kyoto Station Southeast Area, the new center expands the Miami-born art platform into Asia with an expansive, long-term survey exploring human perception.surveys the American artist’s six-decade investigation into light as a physical medium from the 1960s through his contemporary practice. Visitors will encounter immersive installations that transform light from an illuminator into the physical subject itself, spanning early works like his 1966 Afrum-Proto projection—which casts the illusion of a glowing three-dimensional cube into a wall corner—to his renowned Skyspaces, Ganzfelds, and research connected to Roden Crater, his monumental naked-eye celestial observatory inside an extinct Arizona volcano.Designed by teamLab Architects, the Superblue Kyoto venue mirrors its neighbor with a distinct indigo-blue exterior, establishing a unified creative nexus within the City of Kyoto's urban revitalization zone. Together with teamLab's largest domestic museum, the two cultural institutions create a walkable district dedicated to large-scale, multisensory contemporary art.Superblue Kyoto is scheduled to open to the public in early 2027, with further details regarding featured artworks and opening dates slated for reveal in December.
